messages:
Alex Carter: Heads up — after the terraform change to route foo-service through an NLB I see healthy targets flapping in staging. Any quick checks I should run?

infra-bot: terraform apply completed by matt-li (run: tf-2026-03-17). Resources changed: kubernetes_service.foo-service (type: LoadBalancer -> NodePort) :white_check_mark:

Sara Nguyen: Which cluster/namespace? staging or prod?

Alex Carter: staging / default-foo. Symptoms: NLB target group shows instances unhealthy, but pods are fine and kube-proxy logs show connection refused on some nodes.

Matt Li: I pushed the change — we switched to NodePort + annotation to let our NLB target instance ports map to nodePort. I think externalTrafficPolicy is still set to Local so nodes without a pod will fail healthchecks.

Jess R.: Yep — Local + NLB healthchecks commonly fail unless you set the healthcheck to the nodePort or ensure every node has a pod. Two quick fixes: set externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster or add the healthcheck annotation so NLB uses the nodePort. Example annotations: 

```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: "TCP"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "traffic-port"
```

Or change to Cluster: externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster — that makes node-level healthchecks succeed because kube-proxy will SNAT to pods.

Alex Carter: Quick question: does the terraform we applied explicitly set the nodePort? I worry about ephemeral nodePort collisions if we redeploy.

Matt Li: Here's the terraform snippet I applied in staging (shortened):

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service" "foo" {
  metadata {
    name = "foo-service"
    annotations = {
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type" = "nlb"
    }
  }
  spec {
    type = "NodePort"
    selector = { app = "foo" }
    port {
      port        = 80
      target_port = 8080
      # node_port omitted -> assigned from range
    }
  }
}
```

Matt Li: I omitted node_port intentionally to keep it dynamic, but that probably caused the healthcheck mismatch.

Sara Nguyen: For staging OK to pick a static nodePort in the module (e.g., 31080) so NLB healthcheck annotation can reference it. For prod we should prefer externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster unless we need client source preservation.

Jess R.: Also add a comment in the terraform module docs: "If using externalTrafficPolicy: Local with NLB, ensure healthcheck-port=traffic-port or pin nodePort and add healthcheck-port annotation."

Alex Carter: I'll roll back the staging change to Cluster for now and open a PR to pin nodePort + add the annotations and docs.

Matt Li: SGTM. Patching service now: `kubectl patch svc foo-service -p '{"spec":{"externalTrafficPolicy":"Cluster"}}'` — I'll watch the target group.

infra-bot: svc/foo-service patched by matt-li.

Alex Carter: Thanks — will follow up with the PR and add a short note for on-call runbooks about this NLB/Local behavior. :thumbsup:

Sara Nguyen: FYI if people run into this in future, also check kube-proxy mode (iptables vs ipvs) — behavior can differ for healthcheck forwarding.

Jess R.: Good call. I'll add a checklist item to the infra docs.

Alex Carter: closing the loop — staging healthy again after patch. :tada:
